page: Amazon Web Services m6g.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton processors. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture operating at 2.5 GHz. Each physical core executes a single thread without hyperthreading, supported by 64 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core alongside a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory configuration consists of 128.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES instructions but lacks x86-specific vector extensions, GPUs, and local storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate reliable multi-core throughput alongside modest single-core execution metrics. In stress-ng evaluations, the m6g.8xlarge registered an average multi-core CPU score of 47614.83 and an average single-core score of 1489.69. Geekbench tests similarly reflect this dynamic, showing an average multi-core score of 11362.0 compared to a lower-tier single-core score of 932.0. Memory bandwidth reached 158.2 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 75.53 GB/sec for writes. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression (20.36 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (7.62 GB/sec) test in the lower performance tiers, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scales cleanly to an average rating of 63.07 GB/sec.

In operational benchmark workloads, the instance delivered solid application throughput across typical mid-tier tasks. Redis SET operations achieved 35.96 million operations per second, static web serving throughput reached 32.42 GB/sec, and PassMark database operations scored 20248.68. Large language model inference speeds on the CPU registered 819.22 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model and 12.96 tokens per second text generation on a medium 7B model. With a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, m6g.8xlarge offers solid qualitative resource efficiency for parallelized scale-out architectures, container fleets, microservices, and web servers, though it is constrained in serial workloads demanding peak single-thread instruction throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs clocked at 2.5 GHz with a non-hyperthreaded 1:1 thread-to-core mapping. The instance provides 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio, alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network capacity. It does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators like GPUs. Benchmark assessments position the instance well for multi-core parallel processing, demonstrated by solid Geekbench multi-core performance, 35.96 million Redis SET operations per second, and 32.42 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Single-threaded instruction efficiency and single-core benchmarks remain comparatively modest. The instance is suited for multi-threaded container clusters, distributed application runtimes, caching layers, and web application deployments.
